title.value: Estimating causal effects with optimization-based methods: A review and empirical comparison
title.justification: The title precisely captures the content and focus of the paper, which is to review and empirically compare optimization-based methods for estimating causal effects.
title.quote: Estimating causal effects with optimization-based methods: A review and empirical comparison

extractions.description: This paper provides a review and empirical comparison of optimization-based methods for estimating causal effects. It discusses the need for causal inference methods in the absence of randomized controlled experiments and describes various optimization-based methods. The authors highlight the flexibility and advantages of optimization models in estimating causal effects, offer a comparative analysis of these methods, and discuss opportunities for further research.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on optimization methods for causal inference in observational studies, which, while potentially applicable in various fields including sustainability, does not directly address Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development themes.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: the main goal of this review paper is to encourage further contributions from the operational research community to the causal inference literature.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not focus on climate or ecological aspects directly and thus does not fit into any predefined Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development categories.
primary_category.quote: we believe that there exist several unaddressed opportunities that operational researchers could contribute with their advanced knowledge of optimization, for the benefits of the applied researchers that use causal inference tools.

primary_sub_category.justification: There is no specific sub-category related to climate or ecological sustainable development discussed in the paper, as its central theme lies elsewhere.
primary_sub_category.quote: In this review paper, we present an overview of the causal inference literature and describe in more detail the optimization-based causal inference methods.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper does not introduce any new Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development category as its primary focus is on methodological aspects of causal inference with optimization.
new_primary_category.quote: Thus, the main goal of this review paper is to encourage further contributions from the operational research community to the causal inference literature.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: No new sub-category related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development is proposed in the paper.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: we do not cover the methods based on neural networks (e.g., Johansson, Shalit, & Sontag, 2016; Shalit, Johansson, & Sontag, 2017; Louizos et al., 2017; Yao et al., 2018; Kallus, 2020 ) even if the training of such neural networks requires optimization.
